tagline: Interactive pattern library for boss encounter designers
aboutDescription: Why Igor Polyakov created the atlas and how its research, interactive models, translations, and open licenses are developed.
aboutIntro: Boss Fight Atlas is an interactive pattern library that helps game designers turn boss mechanics into readable, tunable, and testable systems.
aboutMotivationBody: Boss mechanics are often discussed as memorable examples or advice for players. I wanted a reusable, source-backed language for designers: one that separates the rule from its presentation and connects each pattern to implementation, tuning, counterplay, and testing.
aboutResearchBody: The catalogue starts from observed mechanics and cited sources. Categories are working navigation, not a claim that every game follows one universal taxonomy.
aboutModelsBody: Animations and the Boss Builder turn written ideas into behavior you can inspect, combine, and test.
aboutReviewBody: Eight locales share the same content contract. Automated checks protect structure; factual, design, and language accuracy still require independent human review.
aboutOpenBody: Original text and illustrations are published under CC BY 4.0, and implementation code under MIT, so the work can be studied, cited, and improved.
aboutContactBody: I am Igor Polyakov, a software engineering manager and product-minded engineer. I build systems that connect research, product decisions, and disciplined delivery.
